# Running the notebooks {#sec-running}

## Three ways to use this companion

1. **Read the website.** The live panels run in the browser with no installation.
2. **Run the code in Google Colab.** Every chapter starts with an **Open in Colab** button. Colab is free and runs in the browser;
   you only need a Google account. Use *File → Save a copy in Drive* to keep your changes.
3. **Run it on your computer** with Jupyter, or rebuild the whole book with Quarto.

## Installation

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt     # numpy scipy matplotlib pandas jupyter ipywidgets
quarto preview                      # live preview while editing
quarto render                       # builds _book/ (HTML)
```

Rendering executes every Python cell once. Results are cached in `_freeze/` (`freeze: auto`), so later builds only re-run the
chapters you changed.

## Publishing the website (GitHub Pages)

The source lives at <https://github.com/{{< var github_user >}}/{{< var repo >}}> (folder `{{< var subdir >}}/`) and the site at
<https://{{< var github_user >}}.github.io/{{< var repo >}}/{{< var subdir >}}/>. After editing a chapter:

```bash
cd notebooks && python build_notebooks.py && cd ..         # refresh the notebooks (Colab buttons point to them)
git add -A && git commit -m "Update chapter 5" && git push   # update the source on GitHub
bash ../publish.sh                                         # render and update the website
```

## Regenerating the notebooks

```bash
cd notebooks
python build_notebooks.py
```

The script converts every chapter, adds a setup cell that works both locally and in Colab (it downloads `detlib.py` from
GitHub when running in Colab), and rebuilds `interactive_explorers.ipynb`.

## The `detlib` module

| function | purpose |
|---|---|
| `kT`, `photon_energy_eV`, `wavelength_from_eV`, `cutoff_wavelength`, `varshni`, `dB` | units, photon energies, band gap versus temperature |
| `MATERIALS`, `alpha`, `penetration_depth`, `alpha_direct_model` | absorption coefficients of Si, Ge, GaAs, InP, InGaAsP, InGaAs; generic direct edge |
| `responsivity`, `quantum_efficiency`, `max_qe_point`, `fresnel_T` | QE and responsivity |
| `photocurrent_structure`, `pin_photocurrent` | photocurrent from the device structure |
| `drift_velocity`, `diffusion_time`, `transit_time` | carrier transport (Caughey–Thomas for Si) |
| `ramo_single`, `pin_impulse_response`, `transit_response`, `f3dB`, `junction_capacitance`, `pin_bandwidth` | Shockley–Ramo currents, transit-time and RC bandwidth |
| `IONIZATION`, `chynoweth`, `apd_gain_uniform`, `apd_gain_profile`, `miller_gain` | avalanche multiplication |
| `excess_noise_mcintyre`, `excess_noise_power` | APD excess noise |
| `photoconductive_gain`, `photoconductivity` | photoconductors |
| `A_STAR`, `schottky_dark`, `fowler_qe`, `msm_capacitance`, `phototransistor_bandwidth` | Schottky, MSM, phototransistors |
| `diode_current`, `operating_point`, `rc_cutoff`, `rise_time` | circuits and load line |
| `shot_noise`, `thermal_noise`, `snr`, `nep`, `detectivity`, `p_min_ideal`, `apd_snr`, `apd_optimum_gain` | noise and figures of merit |
| `ber_from_q`, `q_from_ber`, `sensitivity_pin`, `sensitivity_apd`, `sensitivity_preamp`, `quantum_limit` | digital receivers |
| `solar_iv`, `solar_operating_point`, `solar_mpp`, `shockley_queisser` | solar cells |
| `cte_remaining`, `sensor_snr`, `simulate_exposure` | image sensors |

`det_sim.js` contains JavaScript ports of the absorption tables, the drift velocities, the Shockley–Ramo responses, the avalanche gain,
the solar-cell solver (Lambert W), the detailed-balance limit and a seeded random-number generator, used by the live panels. Every
function was checked against the worked examples of the slides (see the "worked example" sections) and against `detlib.py`.
